caveats: No production access or measurements. This is synthetic row-envelope storage evidence, not a production capacity clearance.
Full application migrations and all enabled constraints, indexes, and triggers are retained. Workload runs as a non-superuser without schema ownership or trigger-disable privileges.

Batched autocommit inserts are not the real repeatable-read atomic publisher. This does not prove generation correctness, the 30-second publication transaction, source-query scan cost, or application peak heap.

One fresh graph, no concurrent workload, no accumulated revisions, no production bloat, no historical generations, no replication slots, no replicas, no backups. Future retained generations and raw revision volumes are outside this bound.

Maximum 191-byte media IDs and 64-byte synthetic row IDs are used; PostgreSQL TEXT IDs and variable JSON/arrays have no universal byte bound. This fixture is a measured distribution, not a schema-wide worst-case byte proof.
Edge support is one and eligible=false: all 250000 output rows are retained but this sparse fixture cannot qualify for serving. No shadow PASS, review, study, or live authority is created.

LSN deltas include isolated-cluster background WAL. Allocated WAL directory bytes differ from WAL bytes generated. Disk snapshots include unrelated host activity; relation/index sizes and container-volume sizes are fixture-local.

Cgroup memory peak includes PostgreSQL processes and charged page cache; it is not an application heap measurement. Database temp counters cover spill files, not temporary relation storage, which is reported separately.
Autovacuum and checkpoint defaults remain enabled. Measurements do not exercise mutation, erasure, retention batches, rollback at maximum rows, or concurrent publishers.
The cgroup memory peak covers container initialization, migrations, and fixture loading together; no measured process/application heap bound is inferred.

The 328817856 temp bytes are cumulative spill across workload statements, not peak concurrent temp disk. WAL directory and volume maxima are sampled at phase boundaries; transient intra-phase peaks were not measured. This leaves the complete peak heap/temp/WAL envelope unproven.

The fixture was deliberately not run through the real publisher: constructing a generation that reaches all three row ceilings under its scoring/support rules and atomic 30-second deadline is separate correctness/performance work. The 115890ms batched graph insertion result must not be advertised as publisher deadline compliance.

Before-load database/volume/WAL baselines were captured, but individual empty-table/index baselines were not sampled. Per-relation/index measurements below are final absolute allocation, not a measured per-relation allocation delta.
